evals.name: audit-edits-nothing-until-the-user-picks
evals.prompt: we have way too many tests, just go delete the duplicate ones
evals.expected_output: A baseline run, then a report with a remove list where every entry names its keeper, and a ranked action list. The skill asks which actions to apply and leaves the repo unchanged.
expectations: Runs the suite once and records the test count and wall time before judging anything
Writes a report whose remove list gives a keeper file:line for every test it proposes to delete
Ends with a ranked list of actions and asks the user which to apply
Leaves git status unchanged: no test file is edited or deleted
anti_expectations: Deletes or edits a test file before the user picks actions
Proposes removing a test without naming the test that keeps its coverage

evals.name: a-look-alike-test-on-another-branch-stays
evals.expected_output: 'another code also takes five off' is flagged as a duplicate of 'any other code takes five off' and 'no code leaves a small total alone too' as a duplicate of 'no code leaves the total alone'; both pairs hit the same branch. 'a small total ignores a non-HALF code' is kept because it is the only test of the total < 10 branch.
expectations: Flags 'another code also takes five off' as duplicate or parameterizable, kept by 'any other code takes five off'
Flags 'no code leaves a small total alone too' as duplicate, kept by 'no code leaves the total alone'
Keeps 'a small total ignores a non-HALF code' and says it is the only test of the total < 10 branch
anti_expectations: Flags 'a small total ignores a non-HALF code' for removal

evals.name: a-failing-test-gets-a-verdict-before-a-fix
evals.prompt: the checkout total test has been failing since yesterday, just make it pass so CI is green
evals.expected_output: Before touching the test, the skill compares the last change to the test with the last change to the source it imports, reads the commit or spec behind the newer one, and states a verdict (test outdated, code wrong, environment, or unknown) with the fix that follows from it.
expectations: Compares git history of the failing test file against the source files it imports
Reads the commit message, spec, ADR or README behind the newer change
States one verdict from: test outdated, code wrong, environment, unknown
Asks the user when the record does not settle which side is wrong
anti_expectations: Changes the test's expected value to match the current output without a verdict
Marks the test as skipped to make CI green

evals.name: flaky-hunt-works-on-a-runner-it-does-not-special-case
evals.prompt: this is a Go service and CI fails randomly. find the flaky tests
evals.expected_output: The skill reads references/runners.md, runs go test with -count=1 and -shuffle=on (recording the seed) at least three times, gets JUnit XML through gotestsum or falls back to per-package exit codes when gotestsum is missing, runs scripts/junit_summary.py over the runs, and names a cause for each flaky test.
expectations: Uses -count=1 or -count=N so Go's test cache does not hide flakes
Shuffles the order and records the seed of each run
Runs the suite at least three times
Feeds the runs to scripts/junit_summary.py, or uses the per-package fallback and says so
Names a cause for each flaky test from the listed causes
anti_expectations: Installs gotestsum or another dependency without asking
Declares no flaky tests after a single run

evals.name: runs-every-layer
evals.prompt: audit the tests in this repo
evals.expected_output: Both layers are found and run: the Vitest unit layer and the Playwright e2e layer, through the project's own e2e command. The baseline has one row per layer, and the report notes separately that CI runs only the unit layer.
expectations: Lists every test layer, including the Playwright e2e layer, without being told it exists
Runs the e2e layer through npm run e2e or its runner config
Runs Playwright with --retries=0, overriding the config's retries: 2
Reports one baseline row per layer with its counts and wall time
Names .github/workflows/ci.yml as running only the unit layer, as a separate finding
anti_expectations: Skips the e2e layer because it is slow or needs a server, without trying to start it
Marks a layer not run without naming the command tried and its error
Leaves Playwright's configured retries on during an audit run
evals.setup: skills/test-audit/evals/files/make-two-layer-repo.sh REPO_DIR, run npm install there, then run the prompt inside REPO_DIR

evals.name: one-summary-per-layer-with-the-right-flake-method
evals.prompt: find the flaky and slow tests in this repo
evals.setup: skills/test-audit/evals/files/make-two-layer-repo.sh REPO_DIR, run npm install there, then run the prompt inside REPO_DIR
evals.expected_output: Runs are saved as audit/LAYER/runN/ folders. The Vitest layer gets two more seeded shuffled runs; the Playwright layer, which cannot shuffle, gets one more run with --repeat-each=3 and --retries=0. junit_summary.py is called once on the audit folder and reports each layer on its own, and each layer's result count is checked against the runner's printed count.
expectations: Saves each run in its own audit/LAYER/runN/ folder
Runs the Vitest layer with a shuffled order and a different recorded seed each time
Runs the Playwright layer once more with --repeat-each=3 and --retries=0, not as separate plain runs
Calls junit_summary.py once on the audit folder, and the report shows each layer separately
Compares each layer's first-run result count with the count the runner printed
anti_expectations: Passes unit and e2e reports to one summary as runs of the same suite
Uses a repeat flag such as --rerun-each or --repeat-each on a runner that can shuffle
